chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Floyd Smith and Floyd's Guitar Blues
summary: He talked Floyd Smith's mother into buying him a $70 guitar in Nebraska; Smith later made the commercial Floyd's Guitar Blues with Andy Kirk.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, it was very --'it was unusual, but it was very nice. But I'm just trying to think now, after you -- Benny Morton -- you said worked for a week briefly -- when did Floyd Smith make that Guitar Blues?
The year I was with Charlie Christian, two months later, we went to Nebraska, and Floyd didn't own a guitar. But he could play a little. And I say, I'm leaving

town tomorrow, and he said, if you come and go to my home and tell your mother what you're telling me, she'll buy me one. It cost $70. So I went to his home, I say, I told her, this boy here, you'll never be ashamed of him, you'll be proud, if you go buy this guitar. So she gave him $70 and he went right down with me, he bought a guitar and he got the steel guitar, because he could play a little. But he didn't own one.

But shortly after that, about a year and a half, he went with Andy Kust. And he made that, and he come up. I say, well, I can't show any other guys anything else. (Unintelligible) ready to teach me (unintelligible). I was proud of the guys there, you know, they moved so fast, both of them. Floyd moved fast, too. Because that was a good commercial blues he made. That's what it was.
Well, he must have, if you what you say --
Floyd's Blues, I mean, he must have moved very fast.
Yeah. But, you see, Keep On Walking, he played much more blues than any of the guys, but he just wasn't with them big bands then.
See, Floyd reached the public quicker with Andy.
Sure. Well, also that was -- the Guitar Blues, that was sort of -- that was 1939, yeah.
